title.raw: 卷二十三 志第十三 天文一 Volume 23 Treatises 13: Astronomy 1

sentences.zh: 志第十三 天文一

translations.literal: Treatise 13: Astronomy 1
translations.idiomatic: Treatise Thirteen: Astronomy, Part One

sentences.zh: 言天者有三家，一曰宣夜，二曰蓋天，三曰渾天，而天之正體，經無前說，馬《書》、班《志》，又闕其文。

translations.literal: Those who speak of Heaven belong to three schools: first Xuanye, second Gaitian, third Huntian; yet Heaven's true form has no prior exposition in the classics, and in Ma Rong's commentary and Ban Gu's treatise the text is likewise missing.
translations.idiomatic: Writers on the cosmos fall into three traditions—Xuanye, Gaitian, and Huntian—yet the classics never settled the true shape of the sky, and neither Ma Rong's Shangshu commentary nor Ban Gu's astronomical monograph preserves an earlier account.

sentences.zh: 漢靈帝議郎蔡邕于朔方上書曰：「論天體者三家，宣夜之學，絕無師法。

translations.literal: Consultation Gentleman Cai Yong of Emperor Ling of Han, writing from Shuofang, submitted a memorial saying: "Those who discuss the celestial body are three schools; the learning of Xuanye has absolutely no teachers or transmitted method.
translations.idiomatic: From exile in Shuofang, Cai Yong—Consultation Gentleman under Emperor Ling of Han—wrote that cosmology had three schools, but the Xuanye tradition had no living teachers and no line of transmission.

sentences.zh: 《周髀》術數具存，考驗天狀，多所違失。

translations.literal: The Zhou bi's computational methods survive intact, yet when tested against the actual state of Heaven they often contradict and miss.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou bi arithmetic is still extant, but when held against observation it fails in many places.

sentences.zh: 惟渾天僅得其情，今史官所用候台銅儀，則其法也。

translations.literal: Only Huntian nearly captures the reality; the bronze instruments used today by the clerks on the observatory platform follow its method.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Huntian scheme comes close to the facts; the bronze armillary on the observatory terrace in use among historians today is built on that design.

sentences.zh: 立八尺圓體，而具天地之形，以正黃道；

translations.literal: They erect an eight-foot sphere showing the forms of Heaven and Earth, to align the Yellow Road;
translations.idiomatic: An eight-foot globe models Heaven and Earth together and fixes the ecliptic;

sentences.zh: 占察發斂，以行日月，以步五緯，精微深妙，百世不易之道也。

translations.literal: to observe waxing and waning, to move the sun and moon, and to pace the five planets—subtle, profound, and refined, a Way unchanged through a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: tracks the seasons, carries sun and moon, and steps the five wanderers—a fine, durable system that has not gone out of date for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 官有其器而無本書，前志亦闕而不論。

translations.literal: The office has the instruments but lacks the basic texts, and the earlier treatises are likewise incomplete and do not discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: The bureau owns the hardware without the foundational manuals, and earlier monographs leave the matter undocumented as well.

sentences.zh: 本欲寢伏儀下，思惟微意，按度成數，以著篇章。

translations.literal: I originally intended to work beneath the instrument, ponder its subtle principles, calculate the degrees into numbers, and set them down in chapters.
translations.idiomatic: I had meant to work under the armillary itself, work out its fine principles, derive the numbers from the degrees, and commit them to writing.

sentences.zh: 罪惡無狀，投畀有北，灰滅雨絕，勢路無由。

translations.literal: My guilt is beyond description; cast into the northern wilds, ashes scattered and rain cut off—there is no way forward.
translations.idiomatic: Guilt beyond words has sent me to the northern frontier; like ashes scattered in rain, every avenue is closed.

sentences.zh: 宜問群臣，下及岩穴，知渾天之意者，使述其義。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should question the ministers and extend inquiry to recluses in caves and cliffs; whoever understands the meaning of Huntian should be made to expound its principles.
translations.idiomatic: The court should consult its ministers and reach down to scholars in seclusion—whoever grasps Huntian cosmology should be asked to set out its doctrine.

sentences.zh: 」時閹官用事，邕議不行。

translations.literal: " At that time eunuch officials held power, and Yong's proposal was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: " Eunuch power was ascendant at the time, and Yong's proposal went nowhere.

sentences.zh: 漢末吳人陸績善天文，始推渾天意。

translations.literal: At the end of Han, Lu Ji of Wu was skilled in astronomy and was the first to develop the meaning of Huntian.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Han, Lu Ji of Wu, an expert in astronomy, was the first to work out the Huntian theory in full.

sentences.zh: 王蕃者，盧江人，吳時為中常侍，善數術，傳劉洪《乾象曆》。

translations.literal: Wang Fan was a man of Lujiang; in Wu times he served as Regular Palace Attendant, was skilled in numerology, and transmitted Liu Hong's Supernal Signs Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fan came from Lujiang; under Wu he served as Regular Palace Attendant, excelled in mathematical astronomy, and carried on Liu Hong's Supernal Signs Calendar.

sentences.zh: 依《乾象法》而制渾儀，立論考度曰：

translations.literal: Following the method of the Supernal Signs, he made a armillary sphere and set forth a treatise on measurement, saying:
translations.idiomatic: On the Supernal Signs method he built an armillary sphere and drafted a treatise on measurement that begins:

sentences.zh: 前儒舊說，天地之體，狀如鳥卵，天包地外，猶殼之裹黃也。

translations.literal: The old saying of former scholars is that the body of Heaven and Earth is shaped like a bird's egg: Heaven enwraps Earth outside, just as a shell enfolds the yolk.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier scholars held that Heaven and Earth form a bird's egg—Heaven wraps Earth on the outside as a shell wraps the yolk.

sentences.zh: 周旋無端，其形渾渾然，故曰渾天也。

translations.literal: It revolves without end; its form is perfectly round—hence it is called Huntian, "Spherical Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: It turns without break in a perfectly round form—hence the name Huntian, spherical heaven.

sentences.zh: 周天三百六十五度五百八十九分度之百四十五，半露地上，半在地下。

translations.literal: The circuit of Heaven is 365 and 145/589 degrees; half appears above ground, half lies below ground.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's full circuit is 365 degrees plus 145 parts in 589—half the sphere stands above the earth, half below.

sentences.zh: 其二端謂之南極、北極。

translations.literal: Its two ends are called the South Pole and the North Pole.
translations.idiomatic: Its two pivots are the South Pole and the North Pole.

sentences.zh: 北極出地三十六度，南極入地亦三十六度，兩極相去一百八十二度半強。

translations.literal: The North Pole rises 36 degrees above the ground; the South Pole sinks 36 degrees into the ground as well; the distance between the two poles is 182 and a fraction degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The North Pole stands 36 degrees above the horizon; the South Pole lies 36 degrees below it; the poles are 182-odd degrees apart.

sentences.zh: 繞北極徑七十二度，常見不隱，謂之上規；

translations.literal: Around the North Pole for a diameter of 72 degrees, stars are always visible and never set—this is called the upper visibility circle;
translations.idiomatic: Within 72 degrees of the North Pole stars never set—the upper visibility circle;

sentences.zh: 繞南極七十二度，常隱不見，謂之下規。

translations.literal: around the South Pole for 72 degrees, stars are always hidden and never seen—this is called the lower visibility circle.
translations.idiomatic: within 72 degrees of the South Pole they never rise—the lower visibility circle.

sentences.zh: 赤道帶天之紘，去兩極各九十一度少強。

translations.literal: The Red Road girdles Heaven's equator, 91 and a fraction degrees from each pole.
translations.idiomatic: The equator belts the celestial equator, roughly 91 degrees from either pole.

sentences.zh: 黃道，日之所行也。

translations.literal: The Yellow Road is the path along which the sun travels.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Road—the ecliptic—is the sun's path.

sentences.zh: 半在赤道外，半在赤道內，與赤道東交於角五少弱，西交於奎十四少強。

translations.literal: Half lies outside the equator, half inside; east it meets the equator at Horn 5 and a little less, west at Stride 14 and a little more.
translations.idiomatic: Half lies north of the equator, half south; it crosses the equator east at Horn 5° slightly less and west at Stride 14° slightly more.

sentences.zh: 其出赤道外極遠者，去赤道二十四度，斗二十一度是也。

translations.literal: Where it emerges farthest outside the equator, it is 24 degrees from the equator—Dipper 21 degrees is the case.
translations.idiomatic: Its farthest point north of the equator stands 24 degrees away—at Dipper 21°.

sentences.zh: 其入赤道內極遠者，亦二十四度，井二十五度是也。

translations.literal: Where it enters farthest inside the equator is likewise 24 degrees—Well 25 degrees is the case.
translations.idiomatic: Its farthest point south of the equator is likewise 24 degrees—at Well 25°.

sentences.zh: 日南至在斗二十一度，去極百一十五度少強是也。

translations.literal: The sun's southern limit is at Dipper 21 degrees, 115 and a little more degrees from the pole—this is the case.
translations.idiomatic: The winter solstice sun stands at Dipper 21°, 115-odd degrees from the pole.

sentences.zh: 日最南，去極最遠，故景最長。

translations.literal: The sun is farthest south and farthest from the pole, hence the shadow is longest.
translations.idiomatic: The sun stands at its southernmost and farthest from the pole, so shadows reach their greatest length.

sentences.zh: 黃道斗二十一度，出辰入申，故日亦出辰入申。

translations.literal: The Yellow Road at Dipper 21 degrees rises at Dragon and sets at Monkey—hence the sun also rises at Dragon and sets at Monkey.
translations.idiomatic: At Dipper 21° the ecliptic rises in Dragon and sets in Monkey, so the sun does likewise.

sentences.zh: 日晝行地上百四十六度強，故日短；

translations.literal: By day the sun travels 146 and a fraction degrees above the ground, hence the day is short;
translations.idiomatic: By day it travels 146-odd degrees above the horizon, so daylight is short;

sentences.zh: 夜行地下二百一十九度少弱，故夜長。

translations.literal: by night it travels 219 and a little less degrees below the ground, hence the night is long.
translations.idiomatic: by night 219-odd degrees below, so the night is long.

sentences.zh: 自南至之後，日去極稍近，故景稍短。

translations.literal: After the southern limit, the sun draws slightly nearer the pole, hence the shadow grows slightly shorter.
translations.idiomatic: After the winter solstice the sun creeps nearer the pole and shadows shorten bit by bit.

sentences.zh: 日晝行地上度稍多，故日稍長；

translations.literal: By day it travels slightly more degrees above the ground, hence the day grows slightly longer;
translations.idiomatic: Its daytime arc lengthens slightly, so days grow a little longer;

sentences.zh: 夜行地下度稍少，故夜稍短。

translations.literal: by night it travels slightly fewer degrees below the ground, hence the night grows slightly shorter.
translations.idiomatic: its nighttime arc shortens, and nights ease accordingly.

sentences.zh: 日所在度稍北，故日稍北，以至於夏至，日在井二十五度，去極六十七度少強，是日最北，去極最近，景最短。

translations.literal: The degree where the sun stands moves slightly north, hence the sun moves slightly north; reaching the summer solstice, the sun is at Well 25 degrees, 67 and a little more degrees from the pole—then the sun is farthest north, nearest the pole, and the shadow shortest.
translations.idiomatic: The sun's position drifts northward, and with it sunrise and sunset; at the summer solstice it stands at Well 25°, only 67-odd degrees from the pole—its northernmost, closest approach, when shadows are shortest.

sentences.zh: 黃道井二十五度，出寅入戌，故日亦出寅入戌。

translations.literal: The Yellow Road at Well 25 degrees rises at Tiger and sets at Dog—hence the sun also rises at Tiger and sets at Dog.
translations.idiomatic: At Well 25° the ecliptic rises in Tiger and sets in Dog, and the sun follows suit.

sentences.zh: 日晝行地上二百一十九度少弱，故日長；

translations.literal: By day the sun travels 219 and a little less degrees above the ground, hence the day is long;
translations.idiomatic: By day it travels 219-odd degrees above the horizon, so daylight is long;

sentences.zh: 夜行地下百四十六度強，故夜短。

translations.literal: by night it travels 146 and a fraction degrees below the ground, hence the night is short.
translations.idiomatic: by night only 146-odd degrees below, so the night is short.

sentences.zh: 自夏至之後，日去極稍遠，故景稍長。

translations.literal: After the summer solstice, the sun draws slightly farther from the pole, hence the shadow grows slightly longer.
translations.idiomatic: After the summer solstice the sun retreats from the pole and shadows lengthen again.

sentences.zh: 日晝行地上度稍少，故日稍短；

translations.literal: By day it travels slightly fewer degrees above the ground, hence the day grows slightly shorter;
translations.idiomatic: Daytime arcs shrink, so days shorten;

sentences.zh: 夜行地下度稍多，故夜稍長。

translations.literal: by night it travels slightly more degrees below the ground, hence the night grows slightly longer.
translations.idiomatic: night arcs expand, and nights lengthen in turn.

sentences.zh: 日所在度稍南，故日出入稍南，以至於南至而復初焉。

translations.literal: The degree where the sun stands moves slightly south, hence its rising and setting move slightly south, until at the southern limit it returns to the beginning.
translations.idiomatic: The sun's station drifts south, carrying sunrise and sunset southward until the winter solstice restores the cycle.

sentences.zh: 斗二十一，井二十五，南北相覺四十八度。

translations.literal: Dipper 21 and Well 25—north and south perceived as 48 degrees apart.
translations.idiomatic: Dipper 21° and Well 25° mark extremes 48 degrees apart on the ecliptic.

sentences.zh: 春分日，在奎十四少強；

translations.literal: On the spring equinox, the sun is at Stride 14 and a little more;
translations.idiomatic: At the spring equinox the sun stands at Stride 14° slightly more;

sentences.zh: 秋分日，在角五少弱，此黃赤二道之交中也。

translations.literal: on the autumn equinox, at Horn 5 and a little less—this is the crossing of the Yellow and Red roads.
translations.idiomatic: at the autumn equinox at Horn 5° slightly less—where the ecliptic crosses the equator.

sentences.zh: 去極俱九十一度少強，南北處斗二十一井二十五之中，故景居二至長短之中。

translations.literal: From the pole in both cases 91 and a little more degrees—north and south midway between Dipper 21 and Well 25—hence the shadow stands midway between the solstitial extremes of length.
translations.idiomatic: Both stand 91-odd degrees from the pole, halfway between the solstitial limits, so shadows fall midway between winter and summer lengths.

sentences.zh: 奎十四，角五，出卯入酉，故日亦出卯入酉。

translations.literal: Stride 14 and Horn 5 rise at Hare and set at Cock—hence the sun also rises at Hare and sets at Cock.
translations.idiomatic: At Stride 14° and Horn 5° the sun rises in Hare and sets in Cock.

sentences.zh: 日晝行地上，夜行地下，俱百八十二度半強。

translations.literal: By day it travels above the ground, by night below—182 and a fraction degrees in each case.
translations.idiomatic: Day and night arcs each span 182-odd degrees above and below the horizon.

sentences.zh: 故日見之漏五十刻，不見之漏五十刻，謂之晝夜同。

translations.literal: Hence the clepsydra for the sun's visibility is 50 marks, for invisibility 50 marks—this is called equal day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Visible and invisible portions each fill fifty clepsydra marks—true parity of day and night.

sentences.zh: 夫天之晝夜，以日出入為分；

translations.literal: Heaven's day and night are divided by the sun's rising and setting;
translations.idiomatic: Astronomical day and night follow the sun's rising and setting;

sentences.zh: 人之晝夜，以昏明為限。

translations.literal: human day and night are bounded by dusk and dawn.
translations.idiomatic: human reckoning uses twilight and dawn as its bounds.

sentences.zh: 日未出二刻半而明，日已入二刻半而昏，故損夜五刻以益晝，是以春秋分之漏晝五十五刻。

translations.literal: The sun is bright two and a half marks before it rises and dusk two and a half marks after it sets; hence five marks are taken from night to add to day—therefore at the spring and autumn equinoxes the clepsydra for day is 55 marks.
translations.idiomatic: Twilight begins two and a half marks before sunrise and ends two and a half after sunset, so five marks shift from night to day—at the equinoxes the daylight clepsydra reads fifty-five marks.

sentences.zh: 三光之行，不必有常，術家以算求之，各有同異，故諸家曆法參差不齊。

translations.literal: The motion of the three luminaries is not necessarily constant; numerologists calculate them by computation, each with agreements and differences—hence the calendrical methods of the various schools are uneven and do not align.
translations.idiomatic: Sun, moon, and stars do not move by fixed rules; mathematicians derive their paths by calculation, and schools disagree—hence calendars diverge.

sentences.zh: 《洛書甄耀度》、《春秋考異郵》皆云周天一百七萬一千里，一度為二千九百三十二里七十一步二尺七寸四分四百八十七分分之三百六十二。

translations.literal: The Luo shu Radiance of Degrees and Spring and Autumn Examination of Strange Correspondences both say the circuit of Heaven is 1,071,000 li; one degree is 2,932 li, 71 bu, 2 chi, 7 cun, 4 fen, and 362 parts in 487 fen.
translations.idiomatic: The Radiance of Degrees and the Examination of Strange Correspondences both give Heaven's circuit as 1,071,000 li and one degree as 2,932 li plus 71 paces, 2 chi, 7 cun, 4 fen, and 362/487 of a fen.

sentences.zh: 陸績云：天東西南北徑三十五萬七千里，此言周三徑一也。

translations.literal: Lu Ji said: Heaven's diameter east-west and north-south is 357,000 li—this speaks of circumference three, diameter one.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji held that Heaven's diameter is 357,000 li, assuming the classic ratio of circumference three to diameter one.

sentences.zh: 考之徑一不啻周三，率周百四十二而徑四十五，則天徑三十三萬九千四百一里一百二十二步三尺二寸一分七十一分分之九。

translations.literal: Examined, diameter one is not merely circumference three; with the ratio circumference 142 to diameter 45, Heaven's diameter is 339,401 li, 122 bu, 3 chi, 2 cun, 1 fen, and 9 parts in 71 fen.
translations.idiomatic: On examination, the ratio is not three to one; with circumference 142 to diameter 45, Heaven's diameter comes to 339,401 li, 122 paces, 3 chi, 2 cun, 1 fen, and 9/71 of a fen.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》：「日至之景，尺有五寸，謂之地中。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou: "At the solstice the shadow is one chi and five cun—this is called the center of the land."
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou states: "At the solstice the shadow measures one chi and five cun—that marks the center of the realm."

sentences.zh: 」鄭眾說：「土圭之長，尺有五寸。

translations.literal: " Zheng Zhong explained: "The earth gnomon is one chi and five cun long.
translations.idiomatic: " Zheng Zhong explained that the earth gnomon is one chi and five cun long.

sentences.zh: 以夏至之日，立八尺之表，其景與土圭等，謂之地中，今潁川陽城地也。

translations.literal: On the day of the summer solstice, erect an eight-chi gnomon; when its shadow equals the earth gnomon, this is called the center of the land—present-day Yangcheng in Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: At the summer solstice, an eight-chi post cast a shadow equal to the gnomon—that defined the center of the land, now Yangcheng in Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 」鄭玄云：「凡日景於地千里而差一寸，景尺有五寸者，南戴日下萬五千里也。

translations.literal: " Zheng Xuan said: "In general, for every thousand li on the ground the sun's shadow differs by one cun; where the shadow is one chi and five cun, south of where the sun stands directly overhead is 15,000 li."
translations.idiomatic: " Zheng Xuan held that shadows shift one cun per thousand li; a shadow of one chi and five cun implies the observer stands 15,000 li south of the subsolar point.

sentences.zh: 」以此推之，日當去其下地八萬里矣。

translations.literal: " By this reckoning, the sun should be 80,000 li from the ground beneath it.
translations.idiomatic: " On that basis the sun lies 80,000 li above the ground below.

sentences.zh: 日邪射陽城，則天徑之半也。

translations.literal: The sun's oblique rays strike Yangcheng—this is half the diameter of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The sun's slanting rays on Yangcheng mark half Heaven's diameter.

sentences.zh: 天體圓如彈丸，地處天之半，而陽城為中，則日春秋冬夏，昏明晝夜，去陽城皆等，無盈縮矣。

translations.literal: Heaven's body is round like a pellet; Earth stands at Heaven's center, and Yangcheng is the midpoint—then in spring, autumn, winter, and summer, dusk, dawn, day, and night, the distance from Yangcheng is equal in all cases, without excess or deficit.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven is a perfect sphere; Earth sits at its center with Yangcheng as the pivot—so in every season, at every hour, the sun's distance from Yangcheng is uniform, without variation.

sentences.zh: 故知從日邪射陽城為天徑之半也。

translations.literal: Hence we know that from the sun's oblique rays on Yangcheng we obtain half Heaven's diameter.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the slanting ray on Yangcheng yields half Heaven's diameter.

sentences.zh: 以句股法言之，傍萬五千里，句也；

translations.literal: Speaking in terms of the gou-gu method, the side of 15,000 li is the gou;
translations.idiomatic: In right-triangle terms, the 15,000-li horizontal leg is the gou;

sentences.zh: 立八萬里，股也；

translations.literal: the upright of 80,000 li is the gu;
translations.idiomatic: the 80,000-li vertical leg is the gu;

sentences.zh: 從日邪射陽城，弦也。

translations.literal: from the sun's oblique rays on Yangcheng is the xian.
translations.idiomatic: the slanting ray to Yangcheng is the hypotenuse.

sentences.zh: 以句股求弦法入之，得八萬一千三百九十四里三十步五尺三寸六分，天徑之半，而地上去天之數也。

translations.literal: Applying the gou-gu method to find the xian, one obtains 81,394 li, 30 bu, 5 chi, 3 cun, 6 fen—half Heaven's diameter, and the number of li from the ground up to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: By the Pythagorean method the hypotenuse comes to 81,394 li, 30 paces, 5 chi, 3 cun, 6 fen—half Heaven's diameter, the height from Earth to the sun.

sentences.zh: 倍之，得十六萬二千七百八十八里六十一步四尺七寸二分，天徑之數也。

translations.literal: Doubled, this yields 162,788 li, 61 bu, 4 chi, 7 cun, 2 fen—the number of Heaven's diameter.
translations.idiomatic: Doubled, that gives 162,788 li, 61 paces, 4 chi, 7 cun, 2 fen for Heaven's full diameter.

sentences.zh: 以周率乘之，徑率約之，得五十一萬三千六百八十七里六十八步一尺八寸二分，周天之數也。

translations.literal: Multiplying by the circumference ratio and reducing by the diameter ratio, one obtains 513,687 li, 68 bu, 1 chi, 8 cun, 2 fen—the number of Heaven's circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Multiplying by pi and reducing by the diameter ratio yields 513,687 li, 68 paces, 1 chi, 8 cun, 2 fen for Heaven's circumference.

sentences.zh: 減《甄耀度》、《考異郵》五十五萬七千三百一十二里有奇。

translations.literal: This is 557,312 and a fraction li less than the Radiance of Degrees and Examination of Strange Correspondences.
translations.idiomatic: That is 557,312-odd li less than the figures in those two texts.

sentences.zh: 一度凡千四百六里百二十四步六寸四分十萬七千五百六十五分分之萬九千三十九，減舊度千五百二十五里二百五十六步三尺三寸二十一萬五千一百三十分分之十六萬七百三十分。

translations.literal: One degree totals 1,406 li, 124 bu, 6 cun, 4 fen, and 19,039 parts in 107,565 fen—1,525 li, 256 bu, 3 chi, 3 cun, and 167,030 parts in 215,130 fen less than the old degree.
translations.idiomatic: One degree equals 1,406 li, 124 paces, 6 cun, 4 fen, and 19,039/107,565 of a fen—1,525 li, 256 paces, 3 chi, 3 cun, and 167,030/215,130 of a fen shorter than the older reckoning.

sentences.zh: 黃赤二道，相與交錯，其間相去二十四度。

translations.literal: The Yellow and Red roads cross each other; the distance between them is 24 degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The ecliptic and equator cross at an angle of 24 degrees.

sentences.zh: 以兩儀推之，二道俱三百六十五度有奇，是以知天體圓如彈丸。

translations.literal: Deducing from the two markers, both roads are 365 and a fraction degrees—hence we know Heaven's body is round like a pellet.
translations.idiomatic: Both circles measure 365-odd degrees by the two-armillary method—proof that Heaven is a perfect sphere.

sentences.zh: 而陸績造渾象，其形如鳥卵，然則黃道應長於赤道矣。

translations.literal: Yet Lu Ji made a armillary globe whose form is like a bird's egg—then the Yellow Road ought to be longer than the Red Road.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Lu Ji's globe was egg-shaped, which would make the ecliptic longer than the equator.

sentences.zh: 績云天東西南北徑三十五萬七千里，然則績亦以天形正圓也。

translations.literal: Ji said Heaven's diameter east-west and north-south is 357,000 li—thus Ji also held Heaven's form to be perfectly round.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji gave Heaven a diameter of 357,000 li, so he too treated the sky as a true sphere.

sentences.zh: 而渾象為鳥卵，則為自相違背。

translations.literal: Yet the armillary globe is a bird's egg—this contradicts itself.
translations.idiomatic: An egg-shaped globe contradicts that assumption.

sentences.zh: 古舊渾象以二分為一度，凡周七尺三寸半分。

translations.literal: The ancient armillary globe took two fen as one degree; its full circuit was seven chi, three cun, and a half fen.
translations.idiomatic: Older globes used two fen per degree and measured seven chi, three and a half cun around the rim.

sentences.zh: 張衡更制，以四分為一度，凡周一丈四尺六寸。

translations.literal: Zhang Heng remade it, taking four fen as one degree; its full circuit was one zhang, four chi, six cun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng rebuilt his at four fen per degree, one zhang four chi six cun in circumference.

sentences.zh: 蕃以古制局小，星辰稠穊；

translations.literal: Fan held that the ancient model's frame was too small and the stars too crowded;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fan found the ancient globe too cramped, its stars crowded together;

sentences.zh: 衡器傷大，難可轉移。

translations.literal: Heng's instrument was excessively large and hard to turn.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng's was unwieldy and hard to rotate.

sentences.zh: 更制渾象，以三分為一度，凡周天一丈九寸五分四分分之三也。

translations.literal: He remade the armillary globe, taking three fen as one degree; its full circuit was one zhang, nine cun, five fen, and three-fourths of four fen.
translations.idiomatic: He built a new globe at three fen per degree, one zhang nine cun five fen and three-quarters of four fen around.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞何承天論渾象體曰：「詳尋前說，因觀渾儀，研求其意，有以悟天形正圓，而水周其下。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief He Chengtian discussed the body of the armillary globe, saying: "Examining in detail the earlier accounts and observing the armillary instrument, I studied their meaning and came to understand that Heaven's form is perfectly round and that water surrounds it below.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief He Chengtian wrote on the globe's design: "Reviewing earlier accounts and inspecting the armillary, I grasped that Heaven is a true sphere with water circling beneath."

sentences.zh: 言四方者，東暘穀，日之所出，西至濛汜，日之所入。

translations.literal: Speaking of the four directions: east is Yanggu, where the sun emerges; west to Mengsi, where the sun enters.
translations.idiomatic: The four quarters are defined by Yang Valley in the east, where the sun rises, and Misty Ford in the west, where it sets.

sentences.zh: 莊子又云：'北溟之魚，化而為鳥，將徙于南溟。

translations.literal: Zhuangzi also said: 'The fish of the Northern Sea transforms into a bird and will migrate to the Southern Sea.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzi tells how the fish of the Northern Deep becomes a bird and migrates to the Southern Deep—

sentences.zh: '斯亦古之遺記，四方皆水證也。

translations.literal: ' This too is an ancient transmitted record—proof that on all four sides there is water.
translations.idiomatic: another ancient record that all four quarters are water.

sentences.zh: 四方皆水，謂之四海。

translations.literal: Water on all four sides is called the Four Seas.
translations.idiomatic: Water on every side—the Four Seas.

sentences.zh: 凡五行相生，水生於金，是故百川發源，皆自山出，由高趣下，歸注於海。

translations.literal: In general, among the five phases metal generates water; hence the hundred streams all issue from mountains, flowing from high to low and pouring into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: In the five-phase cycle metal generates water; rivers rise in mountains, run downhill, and empty into the sea.

sentences.zh: 日為陽精，光耀炎熾，一夜入水，所經燋竭，百川歸注，足於補復，故旱不為減，浸不為益。

translations.literal: The sun is the essence of yang, blazing and scorching; one night it enters the water and scorches dry what it passes; the hundred streams pour in and suffice to replenish—hence drought does not diminish it, nor flooding increase it.
translations.idiomatic: The sun, yang's essence, burns hot; each night it passes through the waters and scorches them, while rivers refill the seas—so drought does not shrink the ocean nor floods swell it.

sentences.zh: 徑天之數，蕃說近之。」

translations.literal: The number of Heaven's diameter—Fan's account comes nearest."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fan's figure for Heaven's diameter comes closest to the truth."

sentences.zh: 太中大夫徐爰曰：「渾儀之制，未詳厥始。

translations.literal: Grand Master of the Palace Xu Yuan said: "The making of the armillary instrument—its origin is not known in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master Xu Yuan wrote: "The armillary's origins are obscure.

sentences.zh: 王蕃言：'《虞書》稱「在璿璣玉衡，以齊七政」。

translations.literal: Wang Fan said: 'The Book of Yu states, "He was at the jade armillary and jade balance, to align the seven regulators."'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fan cited the Book of Yu: 'He attended the jade armillary and jade balance to align the seven regulators.'

sentences.zh: 則今渾天儀日月五星是也。

translations.literal: Then the present Huntian instrument for sun, moon, and five planets is this.
translations.idiomatic: That is the present armillary tracking sun, moon, and the five planets.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄說：「動運為機，持正為衡，皆以玉為之。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan explained: "What moves in rotation is the ji; what holds true is the heng—both are made of jade.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan explained that the rotating part is the ji and the fixed standard the heng, both of jade.

sentences.zh: 視其行度，觀受禪是非也。

translations.literal: Observe their motions and degrees, and watch whether the reception of the Mandate is right or wrong."
translations.idiomatic: By watching their motions one judges whether a transfer of the Mandate is legitimate."

sentences.zh: 」渾儀，羲和氏之舊器，歷代相傳，謂之機衡，其所由來，有原統矣。

translations.literal: " The armillary instrument is the old device of the Xihe clan, transmitted through successive generations and called ji-heng; its origin has a true lineage.
translations.idiomatic: " The armillary descends from the Xihe astronomers, passed down as ji and heng—a lineage with real roots.

sentences.zh: 而斯器設在候台，史官禁密，學者寡得聞見；

translations.literal: Yet this instrument is installed on the observatory terrace; historians guard it in secrecy, and scholars rarely hear or see it;
translations.idiomatic: Yet it sits on the observatory terrace under historians' lock and key, so few scholars ever see it;

sentences.zh: 穿鑿之徒，不解機衡之意，見有七政之言，因以為北斗七星，構造虛文，托之讖緯，史遷、班固，猶尚惑之。

translations.literal: those who force meanings do not understand ji-heng's intent; seeing mention of the seven regulators, they took it to mean the Northern Dipper's seven stars, fabricating empty texts and entrusting them to prognostications—Sima Qian and Ban Gu were still deceived by this.
translations.idiomatic: pedants who never grasped ji and heng seized on 'seven regulators' and invented a tale of the Big Dipper's seven stars, dressing it in prophecy—deceiving even Sima Qian and Ban Gu.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄有贍雅高遠之才，沈靜精妙之思，超然獨見，改正其說，聖人復出，不易斯言矣。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan possessed talent ample, elegant, and far-reaching, and thought deep, tranquil, and subtle; standing alone in insight, he corrected this doctrine—were a sage to appear again, he would not alter this saying.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan, with his ample elegance and subtle penetration, saw through the error alone and set the record straight—a judgment no later sage would overturn.

sentences.zh: '蕃之所云如此。

translations.literal: ' What Fan said was thus.
translations.idiomatic: ' That was Wang Fan's account.

sentences.zh: 夫候審七曜，當以運行為體，設器擬象，焉得定其盈縮，推斯而言，未為通論。

translations.literal: To observe and examine the seven luminaries, one should take motion as the substance; to set up an instrument imitating the image—how can one fix their excess and deficit? Pushing this reasoning, it is not a penetrating theory.
translations.idiomatic: Observing the seven luminaries requires tracking their motion, not a model globe—how can a device fix their waxing and waning? On that logic the argument fails.

sentences.zh: 設使唐、虞之世，已有渾儀，涉曆三代，以為定準，後世聿遵，孰敢非革。

translations.literal: Suppose that in the age of Tang and Yu there already was an armillary instrument, passing through three dynasties as the fixed standard—later ages would all follow it; who would dare reject or change it?
translations.idiomatic: Had the armillary existed under Yao and Shun and served three dynasties as standard, who would dare alter it?

sentences.zh: 而三天之儀，紛然莫辯，至揚雄方難蓋通渾。

translations.literal: Yet the instruments of the three heavens were confused and indistinguishable; only Yang Xiong finally challenged Gaitian and connected Huntian.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the three cosmologies remained tangled until Yang Xiong finally challenged canopy theory and linked it to the sphere model.

sentences.zh: 張衡為太史令，乃鑄銅制範。

translations.literal: Zhang Heng as Grand Astrologer then cast bronze and made models.
translations.idiomatic: As Grand Astrologer, Zhang Heng cast the bronze armillary.

sentences.zh: 衡傳云：'其作渾天儀，考步陰陽，最為詳密。

translations.literal: Heng's biography says: 'In making the Huntian instrument, he examined and paced yin and yang—most detailed and precise.
translations.idiomatic: His biography says he built the Huntian armillary with the most meticulous yin-yang calculations.

sentences.zh: '故知自衡以前，未有斯儀矣。

translations.literal: ' Hence we know that before Heng there was not yet this instrument.
translations.idiomatic: ' So the instrument did not exist before Zhang Heng.

sentences.zh: 蕃又云：'渾天遭秦之亂，師徒喪絕，而失其文，惟渾天儀尚在候台。

translations.literal: Fan also said: 'Huntian suffered Qin's turmoil; teachers and disciples perished and its texts were lost—only the Huntian instrument remained on the observatory terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fan added that Qin's chaos wiped out Huntian texts and teachers, leaving only the armillary on the observatory terrace.

sentences.zh: '案既非舜之璿玉，又不載今儀所造，以緯書為穿鑿，鄭玄為博實，偏信無據，未可承用。

translations.literal: ' Examined, it is neither Shun's jade armillary nor does it record who made the present instrument; taking prognostic texts as forced readings and Zheng Xuan as broadly solid—partial belief without evidence cannot be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: ' It was neither Shun's jade instrument nor does any record name the maker; forcing meaning from apocrypha and treating Zheng Xuan as authoritative rests on no evidence and cannot stand.

sentences.zh: 夫璿玉，貴美之名；

translations.literal: As for xuan-yu, these are names for precious beauty;
translations.idiomatic: Xuan and yu are terms for precious jade;

sentences.zh: 機衡，詳細之目。

translations.literal: ji-heng are detailed designations.
translations.idiomatic: ji and heng are technical terms for its parts.

sentences.zh: 所以先儒以為北斗七星，天綱運轉，聖人仰觀俯察，以審時變焉。」

translations.literal: Hence former scholars took them to mean the Northern Dipper's seven stars, the celestial axis turning—sages looked up and down to examine seasonal change."
translations.idiomatic: Hence earlier scholars mistook them for the Big Dipper's seven stars, the pivot of heaven's motion, through which sages read the seasons."

sentences.zh: 史臣案：設器象，定其恆度，合之則吉，失之則凶，以之占察，有何不可。

translations.literal: The historiographer comments: Set up an instrument's image, fix its constant degrees—when they match, auspicious; when they miss, inauspicious; to use it for observation and divination—what could be impossible?
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer notes: A model with fixed degrees that match heaven brings good fortune and mismatch brings ill—why should observation be impossible?

sentences.zh: 渾文廢絕，故有宣、蓋之論，其術並疏，故後人莫述。

translations.literal: Huntian texts were abandoned and lost, hence there are Xuanye and Gaitian theories; their methods are all loose, hence later men do not expound them.
translations.idiomatic: With Huntian texts lost, Xuanye and Gaitian theories survived, but both are crude and later scholars abandoned them.

sentences.zh: 揚雄《法言》云：「或人問渾天於雄。

translations.literal: Yang Xiong's Fayan says: "Someone asked Xiong about Huntian.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiong's Fayan records someone asking him about Huntian.

sentences.zh: 雄曰：'落下閎營之，鮮于妄人度之，耿中丞象之，幾乎莫之違也'。

translations.literal: Xiong said: 'Luo Xiahong planned it, Xianyu Wangren measured it, Censor-in-Chief Geng modeled it—almost nothing contradicts it.'"
translations.idiomatic: He answered: 'Luo Xiahong designed it, Xianyu Wangren measured it, Censor Geng modeled it—hardly a point of dispute.'"

sentences.zh: 」若問天形定體，渾儀疏密，則雄應以渾儀答之，而舉此三人以對者，則知此三人製造渾儀，以圖晷緯。

translations.literal: " If one asked about Heaven's fixed form or the armillary's density, Xiong should have answered with the armillary; yet he named these three men in reply—hence we know these three made the armillary to chart the gnomon and the warp.
translations.idiomatic: " Had the question been Heaven's shape or the instrument's scale, he would have described the armillary itself; naming these three men shows they built it to map the gnomon shadow and the celestial warp.

sentences.zh: 問者蓋渾儀之疏密，非問渾儀之淺深也。

translations.literal: The questioner was probably asking about the armillary's density, not the armillary's depth.
translations.idiomatic: The question concerned the instrument's precision, not cosmological depth.

sentences.zh: 以此而推，則西漢長安已有其器矣。

translations.literal: Deducing from this, Western Han Chang'an already had this instrument.
translations.idiomatic: On this basis the armillary existed in Western Han Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 將由喪亂亡失，故衡復鑄之乎？

translations.literal: Was it because turmoil and loss destroyed it, that Heng recast it?
translations.idiomatic: Did Zhang Heng recast it only because war had destroyed the original?

sentences.zh: 王蕃又記古渾儀尺度並張衡改制之文，則知斯器非衡始造，明矣。

translations.literal: Wang Fan also recorded the ancient armillary's dimensions and the text of Zhang Heng's remaking—hence we know clearly this instrument was not first made by Heng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fan's record of earlier dimensions and Zhang Heng's redesign proves Heng did not invent the armillary.

sentences.zh: 衡所造渾儀，傳至魏、晉，中華覆敗，沈沒戎虜；

translations.literal: The armillary Heng made was transmitted to Wei and Jin; China fell in ruin and sank among the barbarians;
translations.idiomatic: Heng's armillary passed to Wei and Jin, then was lost when China fell to the barbarians;

sentences.zh: 績、蕃舊器，亦不復存。

translations.literal: the old instruments of Ji and Fan also no longer survive.
translations.idiomatic: and the globes of Lu Ji and Wang Fan vanished as well.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝義熙十四年，高祖平長安，得衡舊器，儀狀雖舉，不綴經星七曜。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Emperor An's Yixi era, the High Ancestor pacified Chang'an and obtained Heng's old instrument; though its form was raised, it did not link the fixed stars and seven luminaries.
translations.idiomatic: In Yixi year 14 the High Ancestor took Chang'an and recovered Heng's armillary, but its fixed stars and planets no longer aligned.

sentences.zh: 文帝元嘉十三年，詔太史令錢樂之更鑄渾儀，徑六尺八分少，周一丈八尺二寸六分少，地在天內，立黃赤二道，南北二極規二十八宿，北斗極星，五分為一度，置日月五星于黃道之上，置立漏刻，以水轉儀，昏明中星，與天相應。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Emperor Wen's Yuanjia era, an edict ordered Grand Astrologer Qian Lezhi to recast the armillary: diameter six chi eight fen and a little less, circumference one zhang eight chi two cun six fen and a little less; Earth inside Heaven; Yellow and Red roads established; north and south polar rings and twenty-eight lodges; Northern Dipper and pole star; five fen per degree; sun, moon, and five planets placed on the Yellow Road; clepsydra marks set up; water turned the instrument; dusk, dawn, and culminating stars corresponded with Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 13 Emperor Wen ordered Qian Lezhi to cast a new armillary six chi eight fen in diameter and one zhang eight chi around, with Earth at the center, ecliptic and equator, polar rings, twenty-eight lodges, the Dipper and pole star, five fen per degree, sun moon and planets on the ecliptic, clepsydra drive, and stars matching the sky at every hour.

sentences.zh: 十七年，又作小渾天，徑二尺二寸，周六尺六寸，以分為一度，安二十八宿中外宮，以白黑珠及黃三色為三家星，日月五星，悉居黃道。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he also made a small Huntian globe, diameter two chi two cun, circumference six chi six cun, one fen per degree; twenty-eight lodges of inner and outer palaces installed; white, black, and yellow beads for the three schools' stars; sun, moon, and five planets all on the Yellow Road.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 he added a small globe two chi two cun across, one fen per degree, with inner and outer palaces marked in white, black, and yellow for the three schools, all luminaries on the ecliptic.

sentences.zh: 蓋天之術，云出周公旦訪之殷商，蓋假託之說也。

translations.literal: The method of Gaitian says it issued from the Duke of Zhou's inquiries of Yin-Shang—likely a spurious attribution.
translations.idiomatic: Gaitian theory claims the Duke of Zhou learned it from the Shang—a likely fabrication.

sentences.zh: 其書號曰周髀。

translations.literal: Its book is titled Zhou bi.
translations.idiomatic: The text is called the Zhou Bi.

sentences.zh: 髀者，表也，周天之數也。

translations.literal: Bi means the gnomon—the number of Heaven's circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Bi means the gnomon—the measure of Heaven's circuit.

sentences.zh: 其術云：「天如覆蓋，地如覆盆，地中高而四隤，日月隨天轉運，隱地之高，以為晝夜也。

translations.literal: Its method says: "Heaven is like an upturned lid, Earth like an inverted basin; Earth is high in the center and slopes on four sides; sun and moon follow Heaven's rotation, hidden by Earth's height—thus day and night."
translations.idiomatic: It holds that heaven is an inverted lid and earth an upturned bowl, highest at the center and sloping outward; sun and moon ride heaven's rotation and hide behind earth's rim to make day and night."

sentences.zh: 天地相去凡八萬里，天地之中，高於外衡六萬里；

translations.literal: Heaven and Earth are 80,000 li apart in all; at the center of Heaven and Earth, one is 60,000 li higher than the outer cord;
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and Earth stand 80,000 li apart; at the world's center the land rises 60,000 li above the outer winter circle;

sentences.zh: 地上之高，高於天之外衡二萬里也。

translations.literal: the height of the ground is 20,000 li higher than Heaven's outer cord.
translations.idiomatic: the central plain stands 20,000 li above heaven's outer ring.

sentences.zh: 」或問蓋天於揚雄。

translations.literal: " Someone asked Yang Xiong about Gaitian.
translations.idiomatic: " Someone asked Yang Xiong about canopy heaven.

sentences.zh: 揚雄曰：「蓋哉！

translations.literal: Yang Xiong said: "A canopy indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiong replied: "A canopy indeed!

sentences.zh: 蓋哉！

translations.literal: A canopy indeed!
translations.idiomatic: A canopy indeed!

sentences.zh: 」難其八事。

translations.literal: " He challenged it on eight points.
translations.idiomatic: " He refuted it in eight arguments.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄又難其二事。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan challenged it on two further points.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan added two more objections.

sentences.zh: 為蓋天之學者，不能通也。

translations.literal: Those who study Gaitian cannot answer through.
translations.idiomatic: Gaitian scholars could not answer them.

sentences.zh: 劉向《五紀》說，《夏曆》以為列宿日月皆西移，列宿疾而日次之，月最遲。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang's Five Regulators states that the Xia Calendar held fixed stars, sun, and moon all shift westward—fixed stars fastest, sun next, moon slowest.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang's Five Regulators reports that the Xia Calendar held stars, sun, and moon all drift westward—stars fastest, sun slower, moon slowest.

sentences.zh: 故日與列宿昏俱入西方；

translations.literal: Hence sun and fixed stars at dusk together enter the west;
translations.idiomatic: At dusk sun and stars set together in the west;

sentences.zh: 後九十一日，是宿在北方；

translations.literal: after ninety-one days that lodge is in the north;
translations.idiomatic: ninety-one days later that lodge stands in the north;

sentences.zh: 又九十一日，是宿在東方；

translations.literal: after another ninety-one days that lodge is in the east;
translations.idiomatic: another ninety-one days and it is in the east;

sentences.zh: 九十一日，在南方。

translations.literal: ninety-one days, in the south.
translations.idiomatic: ninety-one days more, in the south.

sentences.zh: 此明日行遲於列宿也。

translations.literal: This shows the sun's motion is slower than the fixed stars.
translations.idiomatic: This proves the sun moves slower than the fixed stars.

sentences.zh: 月生三日，日入而月見西方；

translations.literal: On the third day after new moon, the sun sets and the moon appears in the west;
translations.idiomatic: Three days after new moon the sun sets while the moon appears in the west;

sentences.zh: 至十五日，日入而月見東方；

translations.literal: by the fifteenth day, the sun sets and the moon appears in the east;
translations.idiomatic: by the fifteenth the sun sets as the moon rises in the east;

sentences.zh: 將晦，日未出，乃見東方。

translations.literal: near last quarter, before the sun rises, it is already seen in the east.
translations.idiomatic: near last quarter it appears in the east before sunrise.

sentences.zh: 以此明月行之遲於日，而皆西行也。

translations.literal: By this it is clear the moon's motion is slower than the sun's, yet all shift westward.
translations.idiomatic: This shows the moon moves slower than the sun, yet all drift westward.

sentences.zh: 向難之以《鴻範傳》曰：「晦而月見西方，謂之朓。

translations.literal: Xiang challenged this with the Hongfan Commentary: "When at last quarter the moon is seen in the west, it is called tiao.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang objected with the Hongfan Commentary: "A moon visible in the west at last quarter is called tiao—swift.

sentences.zh: 朓，疾也。

translations.literal: Tiao means swift.
translations.idiomatic: Tiao means swift.

sentences.zh: 朔而月見東方，謂之側匿。

translations.literal: At new moon when the moon is seen in the east, it is called ce ni.
translations.idiomatic: A moon seen in the east at new moon is ce ni—hiding shyly.

sentences.zh: 側匿，遲不敢進也。

translations.literal: Ce ni means slow, not daring to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Ce ni means slow, reluctant to advance.

sentences.zh: 星辰西行，史官謂之逆行。

translations.literal: When stars and planets move westward, historians call it retrograde motion."
translations.idiomatic: When planets appear to move westward, historians call it retrograde motion."

sentences.zh: 」此三說，《夏曆》皆違之，跡其意，好異者之所作也。

translations.literal: " These three doctrines all contradict the Xia Calendar; tracing their intent, they are the work of those who love novelty.
translations.idiomatic: " All three contradict the Xia Calendar and bear the marks of contrarian theorizing.

sentences.zh: 晉成帝咸康中，會稽虞喜造《安天論》，以為「天高窮於無窮，地深測於不測。

translations.literal: In Emperor Cheng's Xiankang era, Yu Xi of Kuaiji composed the Secure Heaven Treatise, holding that "Heaven's height exhausts the inexhaustible; Earth's depth measures the immeasurable.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Cheng's Xiankang reign, Yu Xi of Kuaiji wrote the Secure Heaven Treatise, arguing that heaven rises without limit and earth sinks beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 地有居靜之體，天有常安之形。

translations.literal: Earth has a body that rests in stillness; Heaven has a form of constant peace.
translations.idiomatic: Earth rests motionless while heaven holds its shape in peace.

sentences.zh: 論其大體，當相覆冒，方則俱方，圓則俱圓，無方圓不同之義也。

translations.literal: Considering their great substance, they should mutually cover and enwrap—if square, both square; if round, both round; there is no meaning in one square and one round."
translations.idiomatic: In substance they must match—both square or both round, not one of each."

sentences.zh: 」喜族祖河間太守聳又立《穹天論》云：「天形穹隆，當如雞子幕，其際周接四海之表，浮乎元氣之上。

translations.literal: " Xi's clansman, Administrator of Hejian Song, also established the Vault Heaven Treatise, saying: "Heaven's form is arched and vaulted, like an eggshell membrane; its rim circles the Four Seas' surface, floating above the primordial vapor.
translations.idiomatic: " Xi's kinsman Song, Administrator of Hejian, proposed Vault Heaven: heaven arches like an eggshell over the Four Seas, floating on primordial vapor.

sentences.zh: 」而吳太常姚信造《昕天論》曰：「嘗覽《漢書》云：冬至日在牽牛，去極遠；

translations.literal: " Wu Grand Master of Ceremonies Yao Xin composed the Dawn Heaven Treatise, saying: "I once read in the Book of Han: at the winter solstice the sun is in Lead Ox, farthest from the pole;
translations.idiomatic: " Wu's Yao Xin wrote Dawn Heaven, citing the Book of Han: at winter solstice the sun stands in Lead Ox, farthest from the pole;

sentences.zh: 夏至日在東井，去極近。

translations.literal: at the summer solstice the sun is in Eastern Well, nearest the pole.
translations.idiomatic: at summer solstice in Eastern Well, nearest the pole.

sentences.zh: 欲以推日之長短，信以太極處二十八宿之中央，雖有遠近，不能相倍。

translations.literal: Wishing to deduce the sun's length of day, Xin believed the supreme pole stands at the center of the twenty-eight lodges; though there is nearness and distance, they cannot differ by a factor of two."
translations.idiomatic: To explain seasonal length he placed the pole at the center of the twenty-eight lodges, holding that distances could not differ by half."

sentences.zh: 」今《昕天》之說，以為「冬至極低，而天運近南。

translations.literal: " The present Dawn Heaven doctrine holds that "at the winter solstice the pole is lowest and heaven's motion draws near the south.
translations.idiomatic: " Dawn Heaven holds that at winter solstice the pole is lowest and heaven's motion leans south,

sentences.zh: 故日去人遠，而斗去人近；

translations.literal: hence the sun is far from people while the Dipper is near;
translations.idiomatic: so the sun stands far from observers while the Dipper draws near;

sentences.zh: 北天氣至，故冰寒也。

translations.literal: northern heaven's qi arrives, hence ice and cold.
translations.idiomatic: northern qi arrives and brings ice and cold.

sentences.zh: 夏至極起，而天運近北，而斗去人遠，日去人近，南天氣至，故炎熱也。

translations.literal: At the summer solstice the pole rises and heaven's motion draws near the north; the Dipper is far from people, the sun near; southern heaven's qi arrives, hence blazing heat.
translations.idiomatic: At summer solstice the pole rises, heaven leans north, the Dipper recedes and the sun draws near, southern qi brings blazing heat.

sentences.zh: 極之立時，日行地中淺，故夜短；

translations.literal: When the pole stands upright, the sun's path through Earth's center is shallow, hence nights are short;
translations.idiomatic: When the pole stands high the sun's underground path is shallow and nights are short;

sentences.zh: 天去地高，故晝長也。

translations.literal: Heaven is far from Earth, hence days are long.
translations.idiomatic: heaven stands far above earth and days are long.

sentences.zh: 極之低時，日行地中深，故夜長；

translations.literal: When the pole is low, the sun's path through Earth's center is deep, hence nights are long;
translations.idiomatic: When the pole is low the underground path deepens and nights lengthen;

sentences.zh: 天去地下淺，故晝短也。

translations.literal: Heaven is shallow above the ground, hence days are short.
translations.idiomatic: heaven lies close above and days shorten.

sentences.zh: 然則天行寒依于渾，夏依于蓋也。

translations.literal: Thus heaven's motion in cold follows Huntian, in summer follows Gaitian."
translations.idiomatic: Thus winter follows Huntian theory and summer follows Gaitian."

sentences.zh: 」按此說應作「軒昂」之「軒」，而作「昕」，所未詳也。

translations.literal: " Examined, this doctrine should use xuan of "lofty and soaring," yet writes xin—it is not clear why.
translations.idiomatic: " The title should use xuan, "lofty," not xin—an unexplained substitution.

sentences.zh: 凡三說，皆好異之談，失之遠矣。

translations.literal: All three doctrines are talk of those who love novelty—far from the mark.
translations.idiomatic: All three are contrarian fantasies, wide of the mark.

sentences.zh: 凡天文經星，常宿中外宮，前史已詳。

translations.literal: As for the fixed stars of astronomy, the constant lodges of inner and outer palaces—earlier histories are already detailed.
translations.idiomatic: Fixed stars and the inner and outer palaces are fully treated in earlier histories.

sentences.zh: 今惟記魏文帝黃初以來星變為《天文志》，以續司馬彪云。

translations.literal: Now we only record star anomalies from Emperor Wen of Wei's Huangchu era onward as the Treatise on Astronomy, to continue Sima Biao.
translations.idiomatic: This treatise records only stellar anomalies from Wei Emperor Wen's Huangchu reign onward, continuing Sima Biao's work.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝黃初三年九月甲辰，客星見太微左掖門內。

translations.literal: In the third year of Huangchu, ninth month, day jiachen, a guest star appeared inside the Left Screen Gate of Supreme Subtlety.
translations.idiomatic: Huangchu year 3, ninth month, day jiachen: a guest star appeared inside the Left Screen Gate of the Supreme Subtlety constellation.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「客星出太微，國有兵喪。

translations.literal: Prognostication says: "When a guest star emerges from Supreme Subtlety, the state has war and mourning."
translations.idiomatic: Prognostication reads: "A guest star in Supreme Subtlety foretells war and mourning for the state."

sentences.zh: 」十月，孫權叛命，帝自南征，前驅臨江，破其將呂範等。

translations.literal: " In the tenth month Sun Quan rebelled; the Emperor personally campaigned south, vanguard reaching the Yangzi, defeating his generals Lü Fan and others.
translations.idiomatic: " In the tenth month Sun Quan rebelled; the Emperor marched south in person, his vanguard reaching the Yangzi and defeating Lü Fan and other generals.

sentences.zh: 是後累有征役。

translations.literal: After this campaigns followed repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigns followed one after another.

sentences.zh: 七年五月，文帝崩。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the seventh year, Emperor Wen died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year seven Emperor Wen died.

sentences.zh: 黃初四年三月癸卯，月犯心大星。

translations.literal: Huangchu year 4, third month, day guimao: the moon encroached on the great star of Heart.
translations.idiomatic: Huangchu 4, third month, day guimao: the moon crossed the great star of Heart.

sentences.zh: 十二月丙子，月又犯心大星。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day bingzi: the moon again encroached on the great star of Heart.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month, day bingzi: the moon again crossed the great star of Heart.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「心為天王，王者惡之。

translations.literal: Prognostication says: "Heart is the celestial king—rulers dread it."
translations.idiomatic: Prognostication reads: "Heart is the celestial king—rulers dread its violation."

sentences.zh: 」七年五月，文帝崩。

translations.literal: " In the fifth month of the seventh year, Emperor Wen died.
translations.idiomatic: " In the fifth month of year seven Emperor Wen died.

sentences.zh: 黃初四年六月甲申，太白晝見。

translations.literal: Huangchu year 4, sixth month, day jiashen: Great White was seen in daylight.
translations.idiomatic: Huangchu 4, sixth month, day jiashen: Venus appeared in daylight.

sentences.zh: 五年十一月辛卯，太白又晝見。

translations.literal: Year 5, eleventh month, day xinmao: Great White was again seen in daylight.
translations.idiomatic: Year 5, eleventh month, day xinmao: Venus again appeared in daylight.

sentences.zh: 案劉向《五紀論》曰：「太白少陰，弱，不得專行，故以己未為界，不得經天而行。

translations.literal: Examining Liu Xiang's Five Regulators Treatise: "Great White is lesser yin, weak, and cannot travel alone; hence with ji-wei as its boundary it cannot cross heaven and travel."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang's Five Regulators Treatise explains: "Venus is lesser yin and weak, unable to travel alone; bounded by ji and wei it cannot cross the sky."

sentences.zh: 經天則晝見，其占為兵，為喪，為不臣，為更王。

translations.literal: When it crosses heaven it is seen by day; its prognostication is war, mourning, disloyal ministers, and change of kings.
translations.idiomatic: When it crosses the sky it appears by day, portending war, mourning, treason, and dynastic change.

sentences.zh: 強國弱，小國強。

translations.literal: Strong states weaken; small states strengthen."
translations.idiomatic: Great powers weaken while lesser ones grow strong."

sentences.zh: 」是時，孫權受魏爵號，而稱兵距守。

translations.literal: " At that time Sun Quan had received Wei's enfeoffment and title, yet raised troops and held out in resistance.
translations.idiomatic: " Sun Quan had accepted Wei titles yet took up arms and held his ground.

sentences.zh: 七年五月，文帝崩。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the seventh year, Emperor Wen died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year seven Emperor Wen died.

sentences.zh: 八月，吳遂圍江夏，寇襄陽，魏江夏太守文聘固守得全。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Wu then besieged Jiangxia and raided Xiangyang; Wei's Administrator of Jiangxia Wen Pin held firm and preserved the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Wu besieged Jiangxia and raided Xiangyang; Wei's Wen Pin, Administrator of Jiangxia, held the city intact.

sentences.zh: 大將軍司馬懿救襄陽，斬吳將張霸。

translations.literal: Grand General Sima Yi relieved Xiangyang and beheaded Wu's general Zhang Ba.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Sima Yi relieved Xiangyang and killed Wu's Zhang Ba.

sentences.zh: 黃初四年十一月，月暈北斗。

translations.literal: Huangchu year 4, eleventh month: the moon haloed the Northern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: Huangchu 4, eleventh month: a lunar halo encircled the Big Dipper.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「有大喪，赦天下。

translations.literal: Prognostication says: "There will be great mourning; amnesty for all under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Prognostication reads: "Great mourning follows; amnesty for the realm."

sentences.zh: 」七年五月，文帝崩，明帝即位，大赦天下。

translations.literal: " In the fifth month of the seventh year, Emperor Wen died; Emperor Ming ascended and granted amnesty to all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: " In the fifth month of year seven Emperor Wen died; Emperor Ming ascended and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 黃初五年十月，歲星入太微，逆行積百三十九日乃出。

translations.literal: Huangchu year 5, tenth month: the Year Star entered Supreme Subtlety, retrograded for 139 days accumulated, then emerged.
translations.idiomatic: Huangchu 5, tenth month: Jupiter entered Supreme Subtlety, retrograded for 139 days, then emerged.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「五星入太微，從右入三十日以上，人主有大憂。

translations.literal: Prognostication says: "When the five planets enter Supreme Subtlety, entering from the right for more than thirty days, the ruler has great anxiety."
translations.idiomatic: Prognostication reads: "When a planet enters Supreme Subtlety from the right for more than thirty days, the ruler faces grave anxiety."

sentences.zh: 」一曰：「有赦至。

translations.literal: " Another reading says: "Amnesty will come."
translations.idiomatic: " Another reading: "Amnesty will follow."

sentences.zh: 」七年五月，文帝崩，明帝即位，大赦天下。

translations.literal: " In the fifth month of the seventh year, Emperor Wen died; Emperor Ming ascended and granted amnesty to all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: " In the fifth month of year seven Emperor Wen died; Emperor Ming ascended and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 黃初六年五月十六日壬戌，熒惑入太微，至二十六日壬申，與歲星相及，俱犯右執法；

translations.literal: Huangchu year 6, fifth month, sixteenth day renxu: Sparkling Deluder entered Supreme Subtlety; by the twenty-sixth day renshen it met the Year Star, both encroaching on the Right Enforcer;
translations.idiomatic: Huangchu 6, fifth month, day 16 renxu: Mars entered Supreme Subtlety; by day 26 renshen it met Jupiter, both crossing the Right Enforcer;

sentences.zh: 至二十七日癸酉，乃出。

translations.literal: By the twenty-seventh day, day guiyou, it then emerged.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-seventh day, day guiyou, it finally emerged.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「從右入三十日以上，人主有大憂。

translations.literal: Prognostication says: "Entering from the right for more than thirty days, the ruler has great anxiety.
translations.idiomatic: Prognostication reads: "When it enters from the right for more than thirty days, the ruler faces grave anxiety.

sentences.zh: 」又「日月五星犯左右執法，大臣有憂。

translations.literal: " Also: "When the sun, moon, and five planets encroach on the Left and Right Enforcers, great ministers have anxiety.
translations.idiomatic: " Also: "When the sun, moon, or planets cross the Left or Right Enforcer, senior ministers face danger.

sentences.zh: 」一曰：「執法者誅。

translations.literal: " Another reading says: "The enforcers are executed.
translations.idiomatic: " Another reading: "Those who enforce the law are put to death.

sentences.zh: 金火尤甚。

translations.literal: Metal and fire were especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: Venus and Mars made the omen especially grave.

sentences.zh: 」十一月，皇子東武陽王鑒薨。

translations.literal: " In the eleventh month, the princely son Prince Jian of Dongwuyang died.
translations.idiomatic: " In the eleventh month Prince Jian of Dongwuyang died.

sentences.zh: 七年正月，驃騎將軍曹洪免為庶人。

translations.literal: First month of the seventh year, Fast Cavalry General Cao Hong was dismissed and made a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year seven Fast Cavalry General Cao Hong was stripped of rank and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 四月，征南大將軍夏侯尚薨。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, General Who Conquers the South Xiahou Shang died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month General Who Conquers the South Xiahou Shang died.

sentences.zh: 五月，文帝崩。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Emperor Wen died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Emperor Wen died.

sentences.zh: 《蜀記》稱：「明帝問黃權曰：'天下鼎立，何地為正？

translations.literal: Records of Shu states: "Emperor Ming asked Huang Quan, saying, 'The realm stands tripartite—where is the seat of legitimacy?
translations.idiomatic: The Records of Shu report that Emperor Ming asked Huang Quan: "Three kingdoms divide the realm—which land holds legitimate sovereignty?

sentences.zh: '對曰：'當驗天文。

translations.literal: He replied, saying, 'One should verify against celestial signs.
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "Examine the heavens.

sentences.zh: 往熒惑守心，而文皇帝崩，吳、蜀無事，此其微也。

translations.literal: Formerly Sparkling Deluder guarded Heart, yet Emperor Wen died while Wu and Shu had no trouble—this is its subtlety.
translations.idiomatic: When Mars last held Heart, Emperor Wen died while Wu and Shu were untouched—that is the subtle point.

sentences.zh: 」案三國史，並無熒惑守心之文，宜是入太微。

translations.literal: " Examining the Three Kingdoms histories, none contain text of Sparkling Deluder guarding Heart; it should be entered Supreme Subtlety.
translations.idiomatic: " Checking the Three Kingdoms records, none mention Mars guarding Heart; he likely meant Mars entering Supreme Subtlety.

sentences.zh: 黃初六年十月乙未，有星孛於少微，曆軒轅。

translations.literal: Huangchu year 6, tenth month, day yiwei: a broom star appeared at Lesser Restraint, traversing Chariot Pivot.
translations.idiomatic: Huangchu 6, tenth month, day yiwei: a comet appeared at Lesser Restraint and passed through Chariot Pivot.

sentences.zh: 案占，孛、彗異狀，其殃一也。

translations.literal: Examining prognostication, broom stars and comets differ in form but their calamities are one.
translations.idiomatic: Per astrological texts, comets and broom stars differ in shape yet share the same portents.

sentences.zh: 為兵喪除舊佈新之象，餘災不盡，為旱凶饑暴疾。

translations.literal: It is the sign of war and mourning, removing the old and laying out the new; if the remaining calamity is not exhausted, there is drought, misery, famine, and sudden pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: They signal war and mourning, overturning the old and installing the new; if the augury is not fully spent, drought, disaster, famine, and plague follow.

sentences.zh: 長大見久災深；

translations.literal: Large and long in appearance means deep, long-lasting calamity;
translations.idiomatic: A large, long-lasting apparition means deeper, longer calamity;

sentences.zh: 短小見速災淺。

translations.literal: small and short in appearance means quick, shallow calamity.
translations.idiomatic: a small, brief one means swift and shallow harm.

sentences.zh: 是時帝軍廣陵，辛丑，親禦甲胄，跨馬觀兵。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor's army was at Guangling; day xinchou, he personally donned armor, mounted a horse, and reviewed the troops.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was camped at Guangling; on day xinchou he donned armor, mounted his horse, and inspected the troops.

sentences.zh: 明年五月，文帝崩。

translations.literal: The next year, fifth month, Emperor Wen died.
translations.idiomatic: The following fifth month Emperor Wen died.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝太和四年十一月壬戌，太白犯歲星。

translations.literal: Wei Emperor Ming, Taihe year 4, eleventh month, day renxu: Great White encroached on the Year Star.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Emperor Ming, Taihe 4, eleventh month, day renxu: Venus crossed Jupiter.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「太白犯五星，有大兵；

translations.literal: Prognostication says: "When Great White encroaches on the five stars, there is great warfare;
translations.idiomatic: Prognostication reads: "When Venus crosses a planet, major war erupts;

sentences.zh: 犯列宿，為小兵。

translations.literal: encroaching on listed lodges means small warfare."
translations.idiomatic: crossing a constellation lodge means lesser conflict."

sentences.zh: 」五年三月，諸葛亮以大眾寇天水，遣大將軍司馬懿距退之。

translations.literal: " Year 5, third month, Zhuge Liang with a great host raided Tianshui; Grand General Sima Yi was sent to repel and drive him back.
translations.idiomatic: " Taihe 5, third month: Zhuge Liang attacked Tianshui with a large force; Grand General Sima Yi was dispatched and drove him back.

sentences.zh: 太和五年五月，熒惑犯房。

translations.literal: Taihe year 5, fifth month: Sparkling Deluder encroached on Encampment.
translations.idiomatic: Taihe 5, fifth month: Mars crossed Encampment.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「房四星，股肱臣將相位也。

translations.literal: Prognostication says: "The four stars of Encampment are the limb-and-bone ministers and the rank of general and chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Prognostication reads: "Encampment's four stars govern the ruler's chief ministers and the posts of general and chancellor.

sentences.zh: 月五星犯守之，將相有憂。

translations.literal: When the moon and five planets encroach on or guard it, generals and chancellors have anxiety."
translations.idiomatic: When the moon or planets cross or hold it, generals and chancellors face danger."

sentences.zh: 」七月，車騎將軍張郃追諸葛亮，為其所害。

translations.literal: " Seventh month, Chariots-and-Cavalry General Zhang He pursued Zhuge Liang and was killed by him.
translations.idiomatic: " In the seventh month Chariots-and-Cavalry General Zhang He pursued Zhuge Liang and was slain.

sentences.zh: 十二月，太尉華歆薨。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, Grand Commandant Hua Xin died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Grand Commandant Hua Xin died.

sentences.zh: 太和五年十一月乙酉，月犯軒轅大星。

translations.literal: Taihe year 5, eleventh month, day yiyou: the moon encroached on the great star of Chariot Pivot.
translations.idiomatic: Taihe 5, eleventh month, day yiyou: the moon crossed the great star of Chariot Pivot.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「女主憂。

translations.literal: Prognostication says: "The chief consort has anxiety.
translations.idiomatic: Prognostication reads: "The empress faces danger.

sentences.zh: 」十二月甲辰，月犯鎮星。

translations.literal: " Twelfth month, day jiachen: the moon encroached on Quelling Star.
translations.idiomatic: " Twelfth month, day jiachen: the moon crossed Saturn.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「女主當之。

translations.literal: Prognostication says: "The chief consort will bear it.
translations.idiomatic: Prognostication reads: "The empress will suffer the blow.

sentences.zh: 」六年三月乙亥，月又犯軒轅大星。

translations.literal: " Year 6, third month, day yihai: the moon again encroached on the great star of Chariot Pivot.
translations.idiomatic: " Taihe 6, third month, day yihai: the moon again crossed the great star of Chariot Pivot.

sentences.zh: 青龍二年十一月乙丑，月又犯鎮星。

translations.literal: Qinglong year 2, eleventh month, day yichou: the moon again encroached on Quelling Star.
translations.idiomatic: Qinglong 2, eleventh month, day yichou: the moon again crossed Saturn.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，太后郭氏崩。

translations.literal: Year 3, first month, Empress Dowager Guo died.
translations.idiomatic: Qinglong 3, first month: Empress Dowager Guo died.

sentences.zh: 明帝青龍二年二月己未，太白犯熒惑。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming, Qinglong year 2, second month, day jiwei: Great White encroached on Sparkling Deluder.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming, Qinglong 2, second month, day jiwei: Venus crossed Mars.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「大兵起，有大戰。

translations.literal: Prognostication says: "Great warfare rises; there is a great battle.
translations.idiomatic: Prognostication reads: "Major war erupts; a great battle follows.

sentences.zh: 」是年四月，諸葛亮據渭南，吳亦起兵應之，魏東西奔命。

translations.literal: " That year, fourth month, Zhuge Liang held the south bank of the Wei River; Wu also raised troops in response, and Wei raced east and west to answer both.
translations.idiomatic: " That year in the fourth month Zhuge Liang held the south Wei River; Wu mobilized in support, and Wei rushed troops east and west.

sentences.zh: 九月，亮卒，軍退，將帥分爭，為魏所破。

translations.literal: Ninth month, Liang died; the army withdrew, commanders quarreled among themselves, and were defeated by Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Liang died; the army retreated, its commanders turned on one another, and Wei crushed them.

sentences.zh: 案占，太白所犯在南，南國敗，在北，北國敗，此宜在熒惑南也。

translations.literal: Examining prognostication: wherever Great White encroaches, if in the south the southern state is defeated, if in the north the northern state is defeated—here it should have been south of Sparkling Deluder.
translations.idiomatic: Per the texts, when Venus strikes a target in the south the southern state falls, in the north the northern state falls—and here Venus should have lain south of Mars.

sentences.zh: 青龍二年三月辛卯，月犯輿鬼。

translations.literal: Qinglong year 2, third month, day xinmao: the moon encroached on Carriage Ghost.
translations.idiomatic: Qinglong 2, third month, day xinmao: the moon crossed Carriage Ghost.

sentences.zh: 輿鬼主斬殺。

translations.literal: Carriage Ghost governs beheading and slaying.
translations.idiomatic: Carriage Ghost governs execution and slaughter.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「民多病，國有憂，又有大臣憂。

translations.literal: Prognostication says: "The people have much illness; the state has anxiety, and great ministers have anxiety too.
translations.idiomatic: Prognostication reads: "The people sicken widely; the state and its senior ministers face disaster.

sentences.zh: 」是年夏，大疫；

translations.literal: " That year in summer, great pestilence;
translations.idiomatic: " That summer a great plague struck;

sentences.zh: 冬，又大病，至三年春乃止。

translations.literal: in winter, again great illness, until spring of year 3 it ceased.
translations.idiomatic: in winter another wave of disease raged until it abated in the spring of year three.

sentences.zh: 正月，太后郭氏崩。

translations.literal: First month, Empress Dowager Guo died.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month Empress Dowager Guo died.

sentences.zh: 四年五月，司徒董昭薨。

translations.literal: Year 4, fifth month, Minister of Works Dong Zhao died.
translations.idiomatic: Qinglong 4, fifth month: Minister of Works Dong Zhao died.

sentences.zh: 青龍二年五月丁亥，太白晝見，積三十餘日。

translations.literal: Qinglong year 2, fifth month, day dinghai: Great White was seen in daylight, lasting more than thirty days accumulated.
translations.idiomatic: Qinglong 2, fifth month, day dinghai: Venus appeared in daylight for more than thirty days.

sentences.zh: 以晷度推之，非秦、魏，則楚也。

translations.literal: Calculating by gnomon and degree, if not Qin or Wei, then it is Chu.
translations.idiomatic: By gnomon reckoning the omen fell not on Qin or Wei but on Chu.

sentences.zh: 是時諸葛亮據渭南，司馬懿與相持。

translations.literal: At that time Zhuge Liang held the south bank of the Wei River; Sima Yi faced him in stalemate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang held the south Wei River while Sima Yi locked horns with him.

sentences.zh: 孫權寇合肥，又遣陸議、孫韶等入淮、沔，帝親東征。

translations.literal: Sun Quan raided Hefei; he also sent Lu Yi, Sun Shao, and others into the Huai and Han rivers; the emperor personally campaigned east.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan attacked Hefei and sent Lu Xun, Sun Shao, and others against the Huai and Han; the emperor marched east in person.

sentences.zh: 蜀本秦地，則為秦、晉及楚兵悉起應占。

translations.literal: Shu is originally Qin territory; thus the armies of Qin, Jin, and Chu all rose, answering the prognostication.
translations.idiomatic: Shu lay in the old Qin domain, and armies of Qin, Jin, and Chu all took the field in fulfillment of the omen.

sentences.zh: 青龍二年七月己巳，月犯楗閉。

translations.literal: Qinglong year 2, seventh month, day jisi: the moon encroached on Door Bolt.
translations.idiomatic: Qinglong 2, seventh month, day jisi: the moon crossed Door Bolt.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「天子崩，又為火災。

translations.literal: Prognostication says: "The Son of Heaven dies; moreover there is fire disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Prognostication reads: "The emperor dies; fire disaster follows.

sentences.zh: 」三年七月，崇華殿災。

translations.literal: " Year 3, seventh month, the Chonghua Palace suffered fire.
translations.idiomatic: " Qinglong 3, seventh month: Chonghua Palace burned.

sentences.zh: 景初三年正月，明帝崩。

translations.literal: Jingchu year 3, first month, Emperor Ming died.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchu 3, first month: Emperor Ming died.

sentences.zh: 青龍二年十月戊寅，月犯太白。

translations.literal: Qinglong year 2, tenth month, day wuyin: the moon encroached on Great White.
translations.idiomatic: Qinglong 2, tenth month, day wuyin: the moon crossed Venus.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「人君死，又為兵。

translations.literal: Prognostication says: "The ruler dies; moreover there is warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Prognostication reads: "The ruler dies; war follows.

sentences.zh: 」景初元年七月，公孫淵叛。

translations.literal: " Jingchu year 1, seventh month, Gongsun Yuan rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: " Jingchu 1, seventh month: Gongsun Yuan rebelled.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，遣司馬懿討之。

translations.literal: Year 2, first month, Sima Yi was sent to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchu 2, first month: Sima Yi was dispatched to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，明帝崩。

translations.literal: Year 3, first month, Emperor Ming died.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchu 3, first month: Emperor Ming died.

sentences.zh: 蜀後主建興十二年，諸葛亮帥大眾伐魏，屯于渭南，有長星赤而芒角，自東北，西南流投亮營，三投再還，往大還小。

translations.literal: Shu Later Lord, Jianxing year 12: Zhuge Liang led a great host to attack Wei and encamped on the south bank of the Wei River; there was a long star, red with horned rays, flowing from the northeast toward the southwest into Liang's camp—it struck three times and returned twice, going large then returning small.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianxing 12 the Shu emperor's general Zhuge Liang marched a great army against Wei and camped on the south Wei River; a long red star with blazing rays swept from the northeast toward the southwest into his camp—three times it plunged in and twice retreated, each pass diminishing.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「兩軍相當，有大流星來走軍上及墜軍中者，皆破敗之征也。

translations.literal: Prognostication says: "When two armies are matched, if a great meteor comes running over the army or falls within the camp, all are signs of defeat and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Prognostication reads: "When armies face each other, a great meteor racing over the lines or falling into camp always presages defeat.

sentences.zh: 」九月，亮卒於軍，焚營而退。

translations.literal: " Ninth month, Liang died in the army; the camp was burned and they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " In the ninth month Liang died in camp; the army burned its fortifications and retreated.

sentences.zh: 群帥交惡，多相誅殘。

translations.literal: The commanders mutually turned hostile, and many were mutually executed and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The generals fell to feuding and killed one another in droves.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝青龍三年六月丁未，鎮星犯井鉞。

translations.literal: Wei Emperor Ming, Qinglong year 3, sixth month, day dingwei: Quelling Star encroached on Well Axe.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Emperor Ming, Qinglong 3, sixth month, day dingwei: Saturn crossed Well Axe.

sentences.zh: 四年閏四月乙巳，復犯。

translations.literal: Year 4, intercalary fourth month, day yisi: again encroached.
translations.idiomatic: Qinglong 4, intercalary fourth month, day yisi: it crossed again.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，太白又犯。

translations.literal: Day wuxu, Great White again encroached.
translations.idiomatic: Day wuxu: Venus crossed it again.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「凡月五星犯井鉞，悉為兵起。

translations.literal: Prognostication says: "Whenever the moon or five planets encroach on Well Axe, all signify warfare rising.
translations.idiomatic: Prognostication reads: "Whenever the moon or planets cross Well Axe, war erupts.

sentences.zh: 」一曰：「斧鉞用，大臣誅。

translations.literal: " Another reading says: "Axe and halberd are deployed; great ministers are executed.
translations.idiomatic: " Another reading: "The axes are drawn; great ministers are put to death.

sentences.zh: 」景初元年，公孫淵叛，司馬懿討滅之。

translations.literal: " Jingchu year 1, Gongsun Yuan rebelled; Sima Yi attacked and destroyed him.
translations.idiomatic: " In Jingchu 1 Gongsun Yuan rebelled and Sima Yi crushed him.

sentences.zh: 青龍三年七月己丑，鎮星犯東井。

translations.literal: Qinglong year 3, seventh month, day jichou: Quelling Star encroached on Eastern Well.
translations.idiomatic: Qinglong 3, seventh month, day jichou: Saturn crossed Eastern Well.

sentences.zh: 四年三月癸卯，在參，又還犯之。

translations.literal: Year 4, third month, day guimao: in Three Stars, again returned and encroached on it.
translations.idiomatic: Qinglong 4, third month, day guimao: while in Three Stars it swung back and crossed again.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「鎮星入井，大人憂。

translations.literal: Prognostication says: "When Quelling Star enters the Well, great persons have anxiety.
translations.idiomatic: Prognostication reads: "When Saturn enters the Well, exalted persons face disaster.

sentences.zh: 行近距為行陰，其占大水，五穀不成。

translations.literal: Traveling near and close is traveling yin; its prognostication is great flood, the five grains do not ripen.
translations.idiomatic: Drawing near is called traveling in yin, portending great floods and failed harvests.

sentences.zh: 」景初元年夏，大水，傷五穀。

translations.literal: " Jingchu year 1 summer, great flood, damaging the five grains.
translations.idiomatic: " Jingchu 1 summer brought catastrophic floods that ruined the crops.

sentences.zh: 九月，皇后毛氏崩。

translations.literal: Ninth month, Empress Mao died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Empress Mao died.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，明帝崩。

translations.literal: Year 3, first month, Emperor Ming died.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchu 3, first month: Emperor Ming died.

sentences.zh: 青龍三年十月壬申，太白晝見在尾，曆二百餘日恆見。

translations.literal: Qinglong year 3, tenth month, day renshen: Great White was seen in daylight in Tail, passing more than two hundred days constantly visible.
translations.idiomatic: Qinglong 3, tenth month, day renshen: Venus appeared by day in Tail and remained visible for more than two hundred days.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「尾為燕，燕臣強，有兵。

translations.literal: Prognostication says: "Tail is Yan; Yan's ministers are strong; there is warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Prognostication reads: "Tail corresponds to Yan—Yan's ministers grow strong and war follows.

sentences.zh: 」青龍四年三月己巳，太白與月俱加丙，晝見。

translations.literal: " Qinglong year 4, third month, day jisi: Great White and the moon together reached bing, seen in daylight.
translations.idiomatic: " Qinglong 4, third month, day jisi: Venus and the moon both reached the bing quadrant and shone by day.

sentences.zh: 月犯太白。

translations.literal: The moon encroached on Great White.
translations.idiomatic: The moon crossed Venus.

sentences.zh: 景初元年七月辛卯，太白又晝見，積二百八十餘日。

translations.literal: Jingchu year 1, seventh month, day xinmao: Great White was again seen in daylight, accumulating more than 280 days.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchu 1, seventh month, day xinmao: Venus again appeared by day for more than 280 days.
